result.title: Yggdrasil: Tree-Routed Recurrent Experts for State Tracking and Fast CPU Inference
result.summary: Parallel-trainable recurrences such as Mamba, linear attention, and DeltaNet offer constant-cost streaming inference, but they suffer from two limitations: 1) they struggle to track discrete state, and 2) they read every parameter at every step, tying model capacity directly to CPU latency. We introduce Yggdrasil, a recurrent architecture that decouples capacity from per-step compute by looking up each layer's transition in a large, tree-routed bank of recurrent experts. Each router addresses its bank using the current token and the state of the layer below. We prove that this cross-layer context is necessary---a single token-indexed layer of non-expanding transitions with finitely many reachable states cannot perform conditional resets---while avoiding feedback from the layer's own past preserves parallel-scan training. Because each step traverses one tree path and reads a single expert per layer, active weights stay within a few hundred kilobytes in CPU L2 cache while the full bank resides in RAM. Among the parallel-trainable models we evaluate, Yggdrasil is the only one to solve all five state-tracking tasks. At matched active parameter counts, it achieves the lowest test bits on enwik8 (1.540 bpb) and the human genome hg38 (1.567 bpb), while stepping $3.0\times$ and $3.3\times$ faster on a single CPU core ($6.7\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $5.8\,μ\mathrm{s}$) than the fastest streaming baseline, and delivering the highest GPU throughput of all models at batch 1024. On the Genomic Benchmarks, it is the strongest causal model at matched active parameters (86.0% mean accuracy).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Yggdrasil，将每层循环转移放入树路由的循环专家库，每步仅沿一条树路径读取单个专家，使模型容量与单步计算解耦；并证明跨层上下文对条件重置是必要的，同时保留并行扫描训练，在状态跟踪任务与 enwik8/hg38 上评测并强调 CPU 推理效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其循环状态转移、条件重置、稀疏专家路由与「活跃权重小、容量大」的设计，可能为 LVR 的 latent 状态更新、动态计算分配及长度泛化提供可核查的架构线索，但属纯文本序列建模，需确认能否迁移到视觉推理状态。
